extracted.intended_audience: mothers, step-mothers, and parents seeking practical child-rearing guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive, domestic-era guidance for mothers/step-mothers on managing children's behavior, training them in household duties, protecting them from adult burdens, and cultivating moral/temperamental development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make yourself love the little ones
rubrics_metrics.description: The first thing for you to do is to begin with your own feelings. Make yourself love the little ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you already love them, half the battle is won. Genuine affection is foundational for success as a step-mother; without it other measures will fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep calm and be firm, steady, yet gentle
rubrics_metrics.description: If a thrill of fear touches him who holds the reins, the horse responds ... This same principle applies to children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be nervous; children detect your inability to control yourself. A firm, steady, yet gentle management is more effective than nervous twitching, threats, or appeals to superior age.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin, continue, and end government with love
rubrics_metrics.description: Their government must have love at its beginning, continuing and ending if it would be successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discipline should be consistently rooted in love rather than purely in authority, harshness, or arbitrary rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add patience, tact, and pity; guard the harsh tongue
rubrics_metrics.description: You have need to add to your love patience, and to that tact, and to that pity. If the children exasperate you, do not let them guess it. Keep a rigid guard upon the harsh tongue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid quick exclamations or scolding lines like 'Stop that noise!' Seal your lips when tempted to be harsh; children remember unjust treatment for years and it undermines attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid correcting children in public or complaining to their father
rubrics_metrics.description: If you can possibly avoid it, do not correct the children in the presence of other people, or complain to their father of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appealing to the father as 'Your mother tells me...' lays foundations of distrust. Better to let them domineer than to show you will manage them by prejudicing the father against them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect children's memory of their deceased mother
rubrics_metrics.description: One way to keep step-children's affection is to talk to them often and reverently of their own mother. Do not allow them to forget her, and guard against the entrance of any jealous feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the children's mother as sacred memory; speak of her reverently and consider the children her charge. This duty helps avoid jealousy and secures the children's trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize disadvantage of the 'step' prefix and compensate
rubrics_metrics.description: You are laboring under a disadvantage in that the hyphenized 'step' must precede your name of mother. ... you have need to add to your love patience, and to that tact, and to that pity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of prejudice against step-mothers, cultivate extra patience and tact; conceal exasperation and avoid giving them grounds to point to unjust acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate tact by perspective-taking
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps the best rule by which to learn it is the old one of 'Put yourself in his place.' Reverse the positions ... imagine yourself a hot-headed, sore-hearted, prejudiced child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly imagine the child's perspective to temper corrections and make tactful patience second nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train children to help with household tasks from early age
rubrics_metrics.description: By the time your child can walk, he may begin to make himself useful. ... One little boy, three years old, finds his chief delight in 'helping mamma.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign age-appropriate tasks (put away toys, hand pillows, dust chair-rungs, pick bits from carpet) to occupy children productively and instill habit of service without converting them into drudges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not overburden children; preserve play and health
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not necessary that your little daughter should become a drudge; that she should have imposed upon her tasks beyond her strength, or which interfere with out-door exercise and merry in-door play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance training with child's need for play and development; duties should prepare for future womanhood/manhood without harming present well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress domestic training as child matures (girls)
rubrics_metrics.description: By the time your girl is ten years old, she should be equal to making her own bed ... dust and keep her own little room in order. ... cultivate an eye for dirt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach line upon line: putting toys away, handing pillows, tucking covers, dusting, making cakes on Saturdays; supervise at first and train attention to household 'hall-marks.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach household economy and value of money (reward competent work)
rubrics_metrics.description: When she is capable of entirely relieving you of this burden, pay her a stated amount each week for doing it. She will glory in ... independence ... and take the first lesson ... of the value of dollars and cents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use small payments for regular tasks (e.g., mending) to teach responsibility, independence, and money management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervise with patience; avoid harsh judgment for carelessness
rubrics_metrics.description: Few children are born with a sensitive conscience regarding their work, so the mother will, at first, find it necessary to keep an eye on all the tasks ... Do not judge her too harshly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember childish carelessness is natural; correct gently, repeat instructions, and reward progress — patience will be rewarded later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach boys domestic skills and neatness too
rubrics_metrics.description: While it is especially expedient that the girls receive this domestic training, the boys of the family should not be exempt ... teach your boy enough of the rudiments of plain sewing ... teach your son that it is his business to keep his own room in order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage boys to darn, sew a little, tidy their rooms, and 'put things to rights' to foster consideration for women and self-reliance; avoid assuming domestic tasks are only for girls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inculcate in boys an 'eye' for order and consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach your son that it is his business to keep his own room in order, and that there is no more reason why his sister should follow him up ... than that he should perform the same office for her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make neatness a duty and a lesson in tender consideration and sympathy for mother, sister, and future wife.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shield children from adult anxieties and financial fears
rubrics_metrics.description: We have no right to make our children old before their time. ... In this 'bit of talk,' I want to enter my protest against thrusting upon children the care-taking thought that should not be theirs for years to come.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not discuss bills, business failures, or household anxieties in ways that frighten children. Teach prudence without feeding them constant fear (examples: child terrified of going to the poorhouse).

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach prudence and economy in age-appropriate manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach your children to be careful, teach them prudence and economy, but let them be taught as children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impart lessons about thrift gradually and simply without imposing the burden of adult decision-making or worry on the child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid forcing child's sympathies or sentimental overuse
rubrics_metrics.description: The forcing of a child's sympathies sometimes produces a hardening effect ... This mother had drawn too often upon her child's sensibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not repeatedly dramatize worst-case scenarios or over-exploit a child's sensibilities; teach empathy without making them prematurely stoic or desensitized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and tolerate 'freshness' of youth; prune and encourage rightly
rubrics_metrics.description: Freshness is almost inseparable from this period ... Young people need training, encouragement and urging in some directions, repression and pruning in others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid blanket condemnation of youthful 'freshness'—provide measured discipline, guidance, and encouragement akin to a gardener training vines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-praising or snubbing; give intelligent appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: If your girl is clever, do not tell her so, or repeat to others in her presence her bright observations. But, on the other hand, do not snub her ... The best way to make a fool of the Young Person is to tell him that he is a fool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise should be balanced and intelligent: encourage without inflating vanity, correct without crushing; stimulate by love and appreciation that is thoughtful rather than blind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model tolerance and charitable speech; parents set the example
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us older people set an example of tolerance and charitable speech. Too often our children are but reproductions ... of ourselves, our virtues, and our faults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate tact, unselfishness, and charity in speech; encourage children to speak kindly or to remain silent when praise is impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train habit of not speaking ill: encourage societies/pledges of kindness
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten girls ... formed a society for the repression of unkind criticism. The members pledged themselves to try ... to speak kindly of people when it was possible ... and when impossible to say nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster concrete practices (pledges, societies) to build the habit of charitable speech and to counteract wholesale intolerance among the young.
